plan.name: Queue each watcher's build checks
plan.summary: Give each watcher one shared queue for plumbing builds' sandbox checks, including test-tool calls in separate MCP processes and fresh factory checks after initial builds, fallbacks and repairs; watch -check-parallel defaults to 1, accepts positive limits for larger machines, and remains independent of -parallel and agent execution. Acquire a place before starting the sandbox's existing deadline, retain it through sandbox cleanup, and release it on success, failure or cancellation; queued calls remain subject to the build's shared execution allowance, are canceled when their build or watcher stops, and cannot bypass an unavailable queue. Publish waiting for checks in the existing build's status and dashboard without changing its run, agent, original start or completion history, restore building when admitted, and retain that waiting reason in the failed build's summary if its own time allowance expires, including during an agent's MCP call. Give queued plumbing jobs enough MCP tool time for their build allowance so the ordinary fifteen-minute tool timer cannot truncate the wait plus checks, while preserving ordinary jobs' defaults, existing sandbox budgets, per-build caches and direct sandbox real-image checks. Update SPEC.md and docs/factory.md with the independent check limit, waiting status and deadline accounting, citing D-0105, D-0113, D-0173, D-0281 and D-0122 as applicable; the merger must record the new #458 decision refining the concurrency and timing policy because this plumbing build cannot write decisions/.

tests.name: TestWatchCheckParallelFlag
tests.says: The watcher exposes -check-parallel with default 1 and rejects nonpositive values before running external tools.

tests.name: TestWatcherBuildChecksShareTheirMCPQueue
tests.says: A test-tool sandbox in a separate MCP process and another build's final sandbox share the same watcher queue in either order, while the second agent can start and both builds pass.

tests.name: TestMCPCheckWaitReportsBuildTimeout
tests.says: A build whose MCP test call waits beyond its own time allowance fails with a waiting-for-checks reason, never starts that sandbox and leaves the queue usable.

tests.name: TestCheckQueueSerializesBuildChecksWithoutChargingSandboxDeadline
tests.says: Two builds share one check slot; the second agent starts while the first checks, and both pass even when the second waits longer than its sandbox deadline.

tests.name: TestCheckQueueConfiguredCapacityAppliesAcrossBuilders
tests.says: A configured capacity of two admits two builds' checks concurrently and makes a third wait until one ends.

tests.name: TestCheckQueueWaitConsumesBuildTimeoutWithoutStartingSandbox
tests.says: A queued build exhausts its own execution allowance, reports waiting for checks and never starts its sandbox, without blocking a later build.

tests.name: TestCheckQueueReleasesFailedAndCanceledChecks
tests.says: Failed and canceled sandbox checks release their slot so a waiting build can finish successfully.

tests.name: TestCheckQueueAlsoCoversRepairedCandidates
tests.says: Review and repair agents can run while another build checks, and fresh checks of a repaired candidate use the same queue.

tests.name: TestFactoryCheckWaitPreservesTheRunningBuild
tests.says: The factory publishes waiting for checks and restores building without changing the run, agent or start time, emitting exactly one real build completion.

tests.name: TestCheckWaitKeepsTheBuildCardAndItsChecks
tests.says: A waiting build keeps its live card, original start, run, agent and completed checks on both dashboard views.

tests.name: TestCheckWaitAppearsInSingleAndParallelHeadlines
tests.says: Single and parallel watcher headlines say which build is waiting for checks and retain the original elapsed-time start.

tests.name: TestCheckWaitTimeoutRemainsAFinishedBuild
tests.says: A build ending while waiting remains a finished build card with its original identity, timing and check history.

tests.name: TestQueuedCheckToolCallsHaveTimeToWait
tests.says: Both agent backends convey the queued job's longer tool allowance with upward rounding, retain ordinary defaults and do not shorten an explicitly larger Codex timeout.
